name: WordCraft One
summary: A Microsoft Word add-in writing assistant with a platform-agnostic analysis engine, local rule checks, an AI provider layer, and a non-destructive suggestion flow.
problem: Writing tools tend to do one of two things: flag everything with no useful replacement, or silently rewrite the document. WordCraft One was built around a stricter contract: every issue must resolve to a real, directly insertable suggestion, and the writer stays in control of every change.
solution: A TypeScript core engine handles grammar, spelling, repetition, and readability, plus an optional AI refinement layer behind a provider abstraction. A React task pane reads the current paragraph through Office.js, shows a writing health score and categorized issues, and lets the writer accept, edit, or reject each suggestion. Accepted changes are written back atomically and remain undoable with Ctrl+Z.
notes: The project keeps the core engine independent of Word so the same analysis layer could serve another editor later.
